problem_motivation.content: Few alloys tolerate metal additive manufacturing thermal cycles.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, only a limited number of existing alloys are amenable to the complex thermal conditions present during metal-based AM

prior_approach.content: Composition adjustment reduced additive-manufacturing microcracks in Hastelloy X.
prior_approach.evidence_span: By increasing the solid solution strengthening elements in the Ni-base superalloy Hastelloy X within the existing commercial alloy composition range, a reduction in microcracking in AM was observed

prior_limitation.content: Rapid gamma-prime precipitation makes high-performance superalloys non-weldable.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, many of the highest-performing Ni-base superalloys are observed to be non-weldable due to the rapid precipitation of the γ ′ phase shortly after solidification

inspiration_source.content: Co-Al-W precipitation strengthening motivated the CoNi alloy design space.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: Recent interest in Co-base superalloys commenced with the study of Sato et al. that revealed the possibility of precipitation strengthening in the Co–Al–W ternary system

causal_claim.content: Segregation lowers local liquidus temperature and creates liquid films.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This solute segregation lowers the local liquidus temperature, creating solute-enriched liquid films between solid dendrites

causal_claim.content: Reduced late-stage segregation improves cracking resistance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The less pronounced segregation in the Co-rich alloys, particularly in the late stages of solidification, is beneficial for cracking resistance

causal_claim.content: Ti, Ta, Nb, and Ni additions improve creep strength in single-crystal variants.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Calculations indicated that Ti, Ta, Nb, and Ni were favorable alloying additions. Creep experiments on several SX variants of these materials confirmed that alloys with these elements possessed creep strengths

causal_claim.content: Repeated EBM thermal excursions can anneal solute segregation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the layer-by-layer thermal excursions in the EBM process might be expected to influence the observed solute segregation

mechanism_principle.content: Near-solidus plasticity makes cracking sensitive to precipitate temperature.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Just below the melting point, stresses can be accommodated by plastic deformation in the solid state, which is very sensitive to the temperature at which the strengthening precipitates appear

hypothesis_statement.content: A solidus-solvus gap over 50 degrees C should resist cracking.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: it was hypothesized that a gap of >50 °C between the solidus and solvus temperatures would increase cracking resistance

evidence_result.content: Both EBM and SLM produced crack-free samples.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The 3D printing trials with both the EBM and SLM approaches resulted in crack-free blocks and blade-shaped samples in the as-printed state
tensile ductilities in excess of 32% are observed for EBM SB-CoNi-10

evidence_result.content: The designed alloy has a 125 degrees C solidus-solvus processing window.
evidence_result.evidence_span: γ ′ -solvus, solidus, and liquidus values for this alloy have been measured by differential thermal analysis as 1204, 1329, and 1381 °C, respectively

evidence_result.content: EBM produces more strongly columnar build-aligned grains than low-preheat SLM.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In the higher preheat EBM process, there is a greater tendency for grains to be columnar and to assume the preferred solidification growth direction of 〈001〉 aligned with the build direction.

evidence_result.content: Hot isostatic pressing removes porosity and recrystallizes the microstructure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: HIP applied above the γ ′ -solvus temperature ( T HIP = 1245 °C) resulted in a microstructure that was free from porosity and also resulted in recrystallization of the microstructure into a coarse-grained equiaxed microstructure

contradiction.content: The high-gamma-prime CoNi alloy remains ductile and crack resistant unlike comparable printed Ni superalloys.
contradiction.evidence_span: The SB-CoNi-10 alloy demonstrates significantly improved ductility and resistance to cracking compared to similar Ni-base superalloys produced by PBF
